title: Special meeting on Stirling Avenue building agreement
subtitle: Emergency services communications direction, a land acquisition review deferral, and closed-session items handled in one short evening.
overview: Council held a short special meeting and spent most of it in a closed session. Council first agreed to meet in camera to consider two solicitor-client matters, a labour relations and personal matter, and a land acquisition matter. One councillor declared a conflict on the strategic land acquisitions review and took no part in it. The transcript indicates that item was handled separately and deferred.

When the meeting reopened, Council directed the Chief Administrative Officer to approve and execute a new, non-binding memorandum of understanding with the Regional Municipality of Waterloo. It covers the operation of the building at 104 Stirling Avenue South, and the CAO must act to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor {{vote:m2}}.

Council also directed staff to proceed as instructed in the closed session on communications response for emergency services {{vote:m3}}. The public minutes give no further detail on that direction. The meeting then passed a confirming by-law and adjourned. No delegations were registered, and the Mayor had no updates.

decisions.detail: The CAO was directed to approve and execute a new, non-binding MOU with the Regional Municipality of Waterloo for operating the building, in line with report COR-2025-087 and to the City Solicitor's satisfaction.
Staff were directed to proceed as instructed in the closed session on communications response for emergency services.

debate: There was no recorded debate on either motion that came out of the closed session. The Mayor asked for discussion on each and none was offered.

A councillor who declared a conflict on the strategic land acquisitions review said the matter could involve properties near ones owned by the councillor's family. The councillor said extra caution was being taken and did not take part.
The transcript shows the land acquisition review was voted on separately from the other closed-session items, with a noted deferral. Council then approved the remaining items for the closed session.
